messages.text: Now cross-check GBTS reconstruction for the single particle cases with the different strixel lengths.

I’ll rerun the established GBTS single-particle benchmark at 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 mm strixel pitch. I’ll keep the geometry, material and reconstruction settings fixed, and check efficiency, fake/duplicate rates and fitted resolutions.

I’m using the ACTS Spack and repository validation workflows again. I found the frozen GBTS benchmark, including the electron and pion cases. I’ll rerun the 0.5 mm control alongside the longer cells and preserve the existing cuts, so the differences measure pitch sensitivity rather than retuning.

The Spack registry still flags changed setup fingerprints, so I’ll verify the actual runtime again before execution. For the main comparison I’ll retain the GBTS benchmark’s frozen Gaussian response, scale only the strixel longitudinal error with length, and leave its fine-coordinate error fixed.

GBTS builds its seeds from pixels, so changing strixel length should mainly affect how the CKF extends and fits those seeds. I’ll cover the established muon, electron and pion cases, using 1,000 events per case for this cross-check and reporting the statistical uncertainty.

The protocol is recorded as an isolated prototype: all five particle/transport populations at 1, 5, 10 and 100 GeV, with all four strixel lengths. Separate implementation and physics-validation agents are checking the runner and assumptions. The response scan will keep the established Gaussian errors and scale only the strixel longitudinal error.

The physics review confirms that 1,000 events per case is useful for screening differences, though it cannot establish very small fake rates: zero fake events would give a 95% upper limit of about 0.3%. I’m also adding hit fingerprints to verify that the different lengths see the same transported particles.

The comparison now has two separate checks: transported-hit records will test sample pairing, while pixel measurements and seeds will test whether digitization changed the GBTS inputs. This matters because larger Gaussian errors can trigger boundary retries and shift later random draws. Any such effect will be reported explicitly.

The independent protocol review supports proceeding with this response study. The original truth-fit evidence remains intact, and its 22 regression tests still pass. The native smoke tests are now running; once they pass, I’ll freeze the runner and launch the full comparison.

The first native smoke test passed: GBTS, CKF, ambiguity resolution and the appended hit writer completed successfully. I’m checking Geant4 and the guarded Fatras electron path next, along with a bridge back to the retained 0.5 mm benchmark.

The retained-data pipeline has passed against the first smoke output, including the independent classifier and every persisted hit branch. I’ve also added a reproducible check that compares each fresh 0.5 mm sample with the same event IDs in the original benchmark.

The four-length muon smoke scan and guarded Fatras electron checks passed. Geant4 electron checks are running now. The full campaign will run three independent, single-threaded cases at a time, scheduling the expensive shower cases early.

The 0.5 mm bridge matches the original retained observables exactly for the muon and Fatras electron smoke samples. That is an encouraging check that the wrapper preserves the baseline behavior; the full campaign will repeat the comparison across all 20 particle/transport/momentum combinations.

All eight native smoke cases passed, including both Geant4 electron lengths, and the Geant4 0.5 mm bridge also matches the original benchmark exactly. The runner is ready for the full scan. I’m finishing the analysis checks and longitudinal-resolution plots before freezing the source.

The source is frozen at `8c45136`, and all 28 new tests pass. I’m launching the full 80-case cross-check now: 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 mm strixels across all established single-particle cases. Geometry, material, field and reconstruction cuts remain fixed.

The campaign is running, and the source review has found no issue that requires stopping it. One statistical refinement is needed: if two lengths reconstruct exactly the same events, the paired bootstrap has zero spread. I’ll add a finite-sample bound so that result cannot be mistaken for proof of equivalence.

Independent checks have confirmed the smoke-test hit pairing and the three 0.5 mm baseline bridges. The current native jobs are the 100 GeV Geant4 electron cases, which are the most expensive shower samples. I’m continuing the source and retained-data checks while they run.

The source review is complete. It found two analysis-only issues, now corrected: zero-change efficiency comparisons carry a finite-sample bound, and measurement-count differences are labeled as net differences. The native simulation and reconstruction files are unchanged, so the running campaign can continue.

The corrected pilot statistics reproduce exactly, and the plots render successfully. The first three 100 GeV electron samples have processed roughly a quarter of their events. I’m keeping the scan unchanged while they finish; this comparison will not be used to retune reconstruction.

The ROOT persistence auditor is ready, with seven tests covering both valid files and adverse cases. It will cross-check saved measurement and track files against the event arrays after the scan. The first 100 GeV electron cases are still progressing without reported native errors.

The repeat workflow is documented now, including native runs, baseline bridges, ROOT checks and plot regeneration. The analysis uses the pinned unrooted revision already in the environment. No shared dependencies have changed.

All 36 implementation and validation tests pass. The first three 100 GeV electron runs are past halfway. I’m monitoring the native jobs; once all 80 cases finish, I’ll run the full comparisons and produce the result tables and plots.

The first 100 GeV electron runs are approaching 1,000 events. After event processing, each run still has to compress and audit its complete output before it counts as finished. The lower-cost particle cases are queued behind these.
The first three 100 GeV Geant4 electron runs have processed all 1,000 events. Their final audits are still running, so I’m not treating them as completed cases yet.

Three full cases have passed their native audits. The 2 mm, 100 GeV Geant4 electron run and the first high-energy Fatras electron runs are now active. I’ll keep their results separate by particle, transport and momentum in the comparison.

The completed high-energy Geant4 cases also pass a direct transport check: all 25 persisted hit columns match bit for bit across 0.5, 1 and 1.5 mm, covering 154,201 hits per case. The 2 mm case is still running; the full analysis will check all four together.

Five cases have passed, and the remaining high-energy Fatras electron cases are well into event processing. No native failures have been reported. The full matrix is still needed before I can give a reliable length-by-length comparison.

All four 100 GeV Fatras electron cases have passed their native audits. I’m using that complete four-length group to check the full-size analysis pipeline while the remaining native cases continue. It is a pipeline check, not the final comparison.

The scan has moved on to the 10 GeV Geant4 electron cases. The full-size Fatras analysis is also running, which will test the variance, pairing and scoring checks on 1,000-event samples before I process the whole matrix.

Reading and checking all candidate states is a substantial part of the analysis time. I’m preparing bounded parallel reduction of independent cases, with an exact comparison against the serial result before using it. The physics definitions and reconstruction settings stay fixed.

The first complete four-length sample has passed analysis. The full single-particle campaign is still running; I’m checking that changing strixel length preserves the simulated hits and that the reconstruction comparisons use the same events.

The 100 GeV Fatras electron sample is complete at all four lengths. Its primary-track efficiency spans 84.6–85.7%, with no duplicate tracks in these samples. I’ll use the paired uncertainties and the remaining particle cases before drawing a conclusion about length dependence.

The checks also cover the stored hit payloads, pixel inputs, seeds, and measurement variances. That matters here because Gaussian retries near sensor boundaries can change later random draws; equal seeds alone would not prove that every reconstruction difference came from the longitudinal response.

The parallel analysis now matches the serial reference exactly: all 316 retained arrays in the four-length pilot, all bootstrap results, and the report text. This lets the remaining analysis run faster while preserving the numerical results.

The 100 GeV Geant4 electron and pion runs have finished at all four lengths, with no execution failures so far. The lower-momentum cases are continuing. I’m now checking transport pairing for the complete high-energy Geant4 electron sample.

The response change remains confined to the strixels’ longitudinal uncertainty; geometry, material, field, seeding, and reconstruction settings are fixed. The reports will include efficiency, resolution, tails, fake tracks, and charge failures separately, so the comparison captures more than changes in the resolution core.

The frozen baseline has known high-momentum electron and pion fit failures. I’m checking charge errors and momentum tails alongside matching efficiency, so the result will show whether longer strixels affect those existing limitations.

All 16 Geant4 electron cases are complete, covering four momenta and four lengths. The campaign is continuing through the pion and muon samples. Transport pairing for the high-energy electron sample is still being checked before I interpret its length dependence.

27 of the 80 native cases are complete, with no failures reported. Their source revision remains identical. I’m keeping that revision fixed until the full matrix finishes so later cases use the same scientific inputs.

The high-energy Geant4 electron sample passes transport pairing: generated particles, transported particles, stored hits, pixel inputs, and seeds agree across lengths. Fine-coordinate strixel and long-strip noise differs in some events, though. I’m making that explicit in the report because those differences also affect how we interpret the comparison.

The 100 GeV Geant4 electron check shows the known momentum problem persists: about 13–14% of matched primaries have the wrong charge at every length, and roughly 55% have a relative pT error above 50%. A successful primary match therefore remains distinct from a good momentum fit in this study.

The Geant4 pion matrix is now complete. The remaining native runs are the muon samples and lower-momentum Fatras electrons. The reporting amendment also passes replay checks: every numerical statistic and bootstrap result remains unchanged.

The campaign has passed halfway, and all four 100 GeV Geant4 muon runs are complete. I’m analysing those now to check the longitudinal-resolution change in the cleaner muon sample while the remaining runs finish.

The first 100 GeV Geant4 muon result shows a modest longitudinal penalty: for |η|<1, the z₀ core width increases from 12.3 µm at 0.5 mm to 14.2 µm at 2 mm, about 15%. Full-sample primary efficiency is 98.7% versus 98.9%. These are preliminary results under the frozen response model; the full matrix and independent review remain pending.

50 cases are complete, with two Geant4 runs left. I’ve also added the portable checks and plot replay to the existing CI workflow, so future changes can check the retained comparison without running ACTS or Geant4. That CI step has not run remotely yet.

All 48 Geant4 cases have completed without execution failures; the remaining runs use Fatras. The earlier truth-tracking study also passes its source and retained-statistics audit, confirming that its evidence remains intact.

61 cases are complete, with no failures reported. The high-energy electron and muon pilots also reproduce all 42 original baseline observables exactly for the same 1,000 event IDs, including NaN masks. The full 20-sample baseline comparison will follow after retention.

Only the final Fatras muon cases remain. Once they finish, I’ll check the complete native matrix, retain the portable results, run the baseline and ROOT audits, and produce the final plots. The repeat commands and validation checks are documented.

All 80 native runs have finished successfully. I’m now checking the complete output set and retaining the portable results. The final review will cover all particle and momentum cases, including charge and momentum tails.

Retention has reached 40 cases with no errors reported. Each case goes through the frozen classifier and response checks before its portable arrays are written. Once the complete inventory is ready, the baseline and ROOT audits can run alongside the statistical analysis.
Retention is processing the large 100 GeV Geant4 electron audit files. I’m also preparing the PDF validation workflow to inspect the final exports, including labels, units, intervals, and rendering.

The large electron files have finished enough checks for retention to advance to 56 cases. The final statistics will use each pitch’s successful tracks and a separate common-success sample, which helps expose changes caused by tracks entering or leaving the matched sample.
All 80 cases are now retained. The paired statistical analysis is running, and I’m starting the full 20-sample baseline comparison and ROOT persistence audit alongside it.

The ROOT audit caught a JSON hashing bug in the new audit wrapper. The stored summary bytes match their original hashes, but re-encoding integer PDG keys changes their order. I’m fixing the comparison and adding regression tests; the native results remain unchanged.

The audit fix passes all 49 focused tests, including a check that altered summary bytes are still rejected. The full baseline comparison passes for all 20 samples, and the ROOT audit has restarted with the corrected comparison.

The full ROOT audit now passes for all 80 cases: event coverage, measurement and candidate counts, persisted variances, and matched-track parameters agree. The baseline comparison also passes. I’m running the ROOT audit replay while the bootstrap analysis finishes.

The complete statistical report is ready for all 80 cases and 20 paired groups. I’m replaying the statistics for an exact match and generating the final unrooted plots. Then I’ll prepare the comparison table for independent review.

The full sample shows a central 100 GeV muon z₀ penalty of 10.6% in Fatras and 15.1% in Geant4 at 2 mm. I’m using the write-page guidance to save the repository summary, while checking the final figure exports. The replay and independent review are still pending.

The final 40 PNG/PDF files reproduce byte-for-byte, and the rendered PDFs pass the visual checks. The complete baseline and ROOT audits, including ROOT replay, also pass. The remaining steps are statistical replay and independent review of the committed evidence.

The exact replay passed for every point statistic, all 400-bootstrap results, and the generated report. I’m committing the evidence locally and sending that exact revision for an independent physics review, including the response qualification, uncertainty treatment, and unresolved momentum failures.
The evidence is committed at `a986756`, and the independent reviewer is checking that exact revision. I’m opening the summary so you can inspect the tables and plots while the review runs.

The 80-case cross-check is complete. At 2 mm, the central 100 GeV muon \(z_0\) core is about 11–15% wider than at 0.5 mm. The independent reviewer is checking the committed results before I close out the study.

The comparisons use identical transport hits and pixel seed inputs across lengths. This tests how the GBTS-seeded track fit responds to coarser longitudinal measurements. The report also retains the high-energy momentum tails, which remain substantial even when a track is successfully matched.

The reviewer has independently passed all 49 tests and the 20 baseline comparisons, and verified the retained data and figure hashes. The remaining check recomputes the reported metrics and selected uncertainty intervals directly from the event arrays.

The scan scales the existing Gaussian strixel response while keeping geometry and material fixed. It measures the reconstruction trade-off under that model; cable and power savings from the earlier estimate have not been folded into the material model.

The independent numerical checks passed: over 1.27 million point values, the paired efficiency intervals, and the central muon resolution intervals reproduce exactly. No material discrepancy was found. I’m recording the review and closing the study locally.

The review is complete with no unresolved material findings. The repeatable workflow, tables and plots are saved, and the project records validate. I’m making the final local closeout commit; the scientific results are unchanged from the reviewed revision.

Completed **80 configurations × 1,000 paired events**: four strixel lengths, \(p_T=1,5,10,100\) GeV, Fatras μ/e and Geant4 μ/e/π, at constant 3 T.

For **100 GeV muons, \(|η|<1\)**, the reconstructed track \(z_0\) core width is:

| Strixel length | Fatras [µm] | Geant4 [µm] |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.5 mm | 13.03 | 12.32 |
| 1 mm | 14.29 | 13.50 |
| 1.5 mm | 14.44 | 13.74 |
| 2 mm | 14.41 | 14.18 |

At **2 mm**, that is **10.6% wider in Fatras and 15.1% in Geant4**. Observed muon matching efficiencies changed by 0 to +0.5 percentage points. Pixel-only GBTS seeds remained identical; the differences arise downstream in track reconstruction.

Existing high-energy fit problems persist, especially for electrons: approximately 13% wrong charge and 55% with momentum errors above 50%.

This is a **scaled Gaussian-response study**, with fixed geometry/material. Boundary retries also change some non-target smearing draws, limiting causal attribution to longitudinal resolution alone.

All **49 tests**, baseline/ROOT audits and exact replay checks passed. Independent review found no unresolved material issues.
